title: Dedicated geo-lock forensic packager and tenant isolation seal generator
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Build an automated forensic packaging service for Dedicated tenants that produces tamper-evident 'isolation seals' and retention-aware data residency reports. The packager should collect runtime metadata (node IDs, AZ/region, GPU inventory), snapshot tenant routing and storage claims, and export a signed bundle suitable for audits and customer requests. This ticket covers design, a prototype exporter, and integration with the audit-collector pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype exporter creates a gzipped bundle containing: start/end timestamps, node identifiers, VPC/subnet IDs, model variant used, routing policy snapshot, retention config applied, and redaction manifest.
Bundle is signed with the cluster signing key and verifiable via the /compliance/verify API.
Exported bundles are indexed in the evidence-store with metadata searchable by tenant, time range, and region.
Retention settings referenced in the bundle match runtime config and console UI values for the tenant.
End-to-end test that simulates a tenant migration between regions produces two bundles showing before/after geo-lock claims.
Docs added to Confluence with instructions for on-demand and scheduled collection and how to validate a bundle.
Prototype performance impact under load is measured and documented (target <2% added p99 latency for control-plane ops).
technical_notes: We will reuse the existing evidence-exporter queue (ENG-61234) but add a geo-lock manifest schema that records AZ/region assertions without copying customer payloads.
Use sigstore-like signing flow: ephemeral key per export signed by KMS-backed root. Store signature and public cert in evidence-store.
Retention config cross-check will rely on the tenant-config service (read-only) and a snapshot taken at export time to prevent later drift.
Bundle format: tar.gz of JSON documents plus a small index; avoid including raw user data. If user content is required for forensic reasons, require PM/legal approval and a separate workflow.
Prototype in Go; follow existing exporter patterns to make later porting to the audit pipeline straightforward.
We may introduce a new lightweight schema field 'isolation_seal_version' to support future cryptographic proofs.
progress_updates: 2025-02-13: Kickoff meeting — aligned on minimal export schema and sign/verify flow. Decided to avoid raw customer payloads in default bundle.
2025-02-20: Spike complete — prototype can pull node metadata and tenant routing snapshot from control plane. Initial bundle size ~12KB.
2025-02-26: Implemented signing using KMS envelope keys; demoed verifying signature locally. Diego to harden key rotation handling.

2025-03-03: Integration tests added for retention snapshot and bundle indexing. Found edge-case when tenant updates retention during export — added transactionally consistent read in tenant-config service.
2025-03-04: PR opened (see links). Running perf benchmark on staging: <1% p99 increase for control-plane export workflow under synthetic load.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Including raw user payload in bundles increases compliance exposure and storage cost; default is to exclude and provide a gated workflow for full captures.
Signing introduces key management complexity; we must ensure rotated keys do not invalidate older bundles — include signing metadata and certificate chain.
Export generation could be heavy under massive tenant fleets — schedule and rate-limit exports per-tenant and shard exporter workers.
Providing cryptographic 'location proofs' (e.g., TPM-signed node attestations) is out of scope for the prototype and may be a follow-up (security & infra coordination required).
